vectors.description: Canonical handle form and short handle: canonical('m6sc7 n75yr') = 'M6SC7-N75YR'; parseShort('m6sc7') = 'M6SC7'
Short-handle collision: prefixes a1b2c3d4e5f6 and a1b2c3d40000 share the first 25 bits (the short handle M6SC7); both must show the full handle; 010203040506 does not collide
Transport-mask bit 5 (0x20) = 'accepts and sends LABELS'; a base mask 0x01 becomes 0x21; labels flow only if both endpoint hellos carry it; off = hello unchanged
vectors.notes: An opener that did not advertise bit 5 rejects content type 10 as 'Unknown end-to-end content type 10'. A stream hop through an opaque relay (link peer != endpoint peer) sends no LABELS.

Bundled UTS #39 table (assets/uts39/confusables_ma.txt, ~6,700 mappings): skeleton(U+0410) = 'A', skeleton(U+043E) = 'o', skeleton(U+04CF) = 'l'; skeleton('I') == skeleton('l'); an all-Cyrillic look-alike of 'Alice' (U+0410 U+04CF U+0456 U+0441 U+0435) has the same lower-cased skeleton as 'Alice'
vectors.notes: Depends on the exact confusables table shipped (Unicode UTS #39 confusablesSummary 'MA' data; license in assets/third_party_licenses/unicode.txt). A second implementation must use the same table version to match. Other asserted cases: case alone is the same reading ('Alice' ~ 'alice'), capital I and lower l stay confusable ('Ilya' ~ 'llya'), invisible format characters do not change a skeleton, real Cyrillic names with no Latin twin ('Сергей') are not flagged.

vectors.description: Build tag encoding in the link-hello nonce (bytes 0..1, big-endian u16): bit 15 = project release key, bits 14..0 = release number R; (R=1,key=false) -> 0x0001, (1,true) -> 0x8001, (32767,false) -> 0x7fff
vectors.notes: Link hello only, transport-mask bit 7 (0x80) set; remaining nonce bytes 2..31 are random. docs/PROTOCOL.md 'Build tag in the link hello'.

vectors.description: Build tag decode: 0 (release 0), 0x8000 and values above 16 bits are not tags; round trip holds for 1, 2, 12, 300, 0x7fff, 0x8001, 0xffff

Release number from versionCode: code 12 (release key signer) -> release 1 with the key bit; code 20 (other signer) -> release 2 without; code 1 and 9 (non-split/debug) and a switch-off send no tag; codes 10, 11, 12 give the same tag (the ABI digit is dropped)
vectors.notes: R = versionCode / 10 (integer division). docs/PROTOCOL.md line 97.

vectors.description: A tagged link hello sets nonce[0] = 0x80, nonce[1] = 0x07 for (release 7, release key) and ORs transport-mask bit 7; an end-to-end hello never carries a tag; a mask that already uses bit 7 gets no tag

description: Peer labels: Crockford handles, signed labels BNL1 and the LABELS container BLB1, LabelText rules, generated stranger names (names-v1/v2), UTS #39 skeletons, build tag in the link hello nonce. BNL1 = 'BNL1' | 01 | kind(1: 1 name, 2 title, 3 subject) | u16 spki length | SPKI | u32 sequence | binding type(1: 1 call, 2 stream) | binding(16) | u8 text length (1..64) | UTF-8 text | u16 signature length (1..256) | DER ECDSA P-256 SHA-256 signature over 'BluetoothVideoMesh/Label/1' NUL || every byte before the signature length. BLB1 = 'BLB1' | count (0..3) | count x (u16 length | BNL1). LABELS is BME1 content type 10 (packet flags 0), sent only when both endpoint hellos carry transport bit 5 (0x20).
